title.narrative: Project Readines Financing: Tourism Development Project

description.narrative: Tajikistan is recognized as a potential tourism hotspot because of its mountainous topography, natural assets, culture, and history as an important link along the old Silk Road. However, this potential remains largely untapped for various reasons, including poor connectivity, inadequate infrastructure, the absence of a comprehensive tourism ecosystem to ensure quality service delivery, weak institutional and regulatory capacity, and a poor business environment. The government has adopted modest measures to promote tourism, including the introduction of an e-visa system and the provision of tax exemptions for investments in tourism-related facilities such as small hotels and motels, hunting and fishing facilities, and mountaineering infrastructure. However, it has yet to formulate a tourism satellite account (TSA), which is a strategic prerequisite for developing and monitoring the tourism industry in the country and Asian Development Bank (ADB) support is needed to move the government's development efforts to the next level.

description.narrative: Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Output 1 Indicator: Output 1. Tourism development plan prepared. (i) surveys of domestic and international tourists complete, (ii) tourism satellite account established, (iii) tourism master plan prepared Progress/Status: Partially completed (80% complete)
1. Development of a tourism satellite account (TSA). Initial works to establish the TSA commenced in 2020, however several challenges were experienced which delayed the completion of the TSA. It was noted that the approach did not align with the United Nations World Travel Organization's (UNWTO) methodology for the establishment of a TSA, and surveys conducted delivered poor results, due to the quality of data collected and the duration in which the surveys took place (i.e. during the COVID-19 pandemic, and limited to the winter period when tourism activity was low).
To address the deficiency, the CTD recruited an International Consultant on the National Accounts Statistics (Contract Package CS-8b) to support data collection and analysis for the establishment of the TSA. To date, the International Consultant has prepared six out of 10 tables, based on information provided by the CTD, outputs of international and domestic tourist surveys, findings from consultants Hidria Cienca (who prepared tourism master plans for Dushanbe and surrounds), and data from the Agency on statistics under the President Republic of Tajikistan (Tajstats). Actions required to complete the TSA were discussed during the review mission held on 10-14 March 2025.
2. Establishment of a destination management organization (DMO). (Progress: Partially Complete). To date, no work has commenced on the establishment of a DMO. During the review mission in Mar 2025, ADB discussed that deliverable should focus on establishing the CTD as a national tourism organization as there is a critical need to develop the functions of the CTD with essential governance structures, guidance documents, and adequate human and financial resources to oversee the tourism sector for the country. ADB proposed for the CTD to consider implementing the actions outlined by the UNWTO in its Sustainable Tourism Development Plan.
3. Development of tourism plans for heritage sites. (Progress: Complete).
4. Market assessment and skills mapping. (Progress: Partially Complete). The CTD advised that a market assessment was completed as part of the establishment of the TSA which included an assessment on the demands of personal tourists including purpose of visits. The tourism study and master plans developed by the UNWTO and Hidria Cienca also contained information relating to the tourism market and trends. While there were issues with the collection of data, it was discussed that the current data may be sufficient to form the initial basis of the market assessment without the need for additional surveys. CTD to assess and confirm the current information, note any gaps and provide confirmation to the ADB project team if additional works are required to be conducted under the PRF. A labor skills survey is underway and is expected to be completed by June 2025
5. Institutional strengthening and creating an enabling environment. (Progress: Partially Complete). e CTD to consider key actions, based on the list prepared by UNWTO and utilize funds from the PRF to conduct necessary actions to strengthen the institutional and governance arrangement for sustainable tourism, and develop the capacity of CTD.
Actions required to complete this Output were discussed during the review mission held on 10-14 March 2025.

Output: Output 1 Indicator: Output 2: Pipeline of investments developed. Progress/Status: 1. Development of tourism master plans. (Progress: Complete). Two tourism master plans have been developed, which covers: (i) Dushanbe and its surroundings, including parts of the Khatlon Region; and (ii) Sughd Region. The master plans identified over 45 potential projects for development in the regions. Of this, the Government of Tajikistan, CTD and ADB agreed for pre-feasibility studies to be prepared for eight priority investments.
2. Development of pre-feasibility study reports. (Progress: Complete). Pre-feasibility study reports for the eight priority investments have been developed by the consultants. Final reports have been submitted to the CTD and ADB and the consultancy contracts have now been closed.

Output: Output 1 Indicator: Output 3: Investment projects prepared. Progress/Status: Preparation of the Terms of reference for feasibility studies and detailed designs for priority projects will commence upon receipt of the government's proposed piority list and upon ADB's approval of such list, expected by 30 April 2025
